senses.definition: Someone who or something that trails (follows behind); something that is trailing.

quotes.text: There were vehicles following me, of course, but was any of them trailing me? […] Without any warning, and without signalling with the trafficator, I took a sudden right turn, hoping to shake off my trailer.
quotes.reference: 2014, Chris Ekpekurede, Laughing Over Serious Matters: Stories to Make You Laugh and Reflect:

senses.definition: Part of an object which extends some distance beyond the main body of the object.
An unpowered wheeled vehicle (not a caravan or camper) that is towed behind another, and used to carry equipment, etc., that cannot be carried in the leading vehicle.
examples: At the end of the day, we put the snowmobiles back on the trailer.

quotes.text: My trailer is a Highlander T-14 8G, one of the smallest trailers. I normally use it for carrying a pair of Sunfish sailboats that are much lighter than its 800-pound weight limit.
quotes.reference: 1980 April, Greg Stone, “Utility hauling? Do it with your boat trailer”, in Popular Science, page 104:

quotes.text: Or you can slide the trailer′s tandem forward toward the tractor. This changes the kingpin weight because you changed the “A” dimension of the trailer along with its wheel-base.

senses.definition: (US) A furnished vehicle towed behind another, and used as a dwelling when stationary.
examples: We drove our trailer to Yellowstone Park.

senses.definition: (US) A prefabricated home that could be towed to a new destination but is typically permanently left in an area designated for such homes.
examples: The young couple′s first home was in a trailer.

senses.definition: (chiefly US, media) A preview of a film, video game or TV show.
examples: The trailer for that movie makes it seem like it would be fun.

senses.definition: A short blank segment of film at the end of a reel, for convenient insertion of the film in a projector.

(computing) The final record of a list of data items, often identified by a key field with an otherwise invalid value that sorts last alphabetically (e.g., “ZZZZZ”) or numerically (“99999”); especially common in the context of punched cards, where the final card is called a trailer card.
examples: The linked list terminates with a trailer record.

senses.definition: (networking) The last part of a packet, often containing a check sequence.
examples: The encapsulation layer adds an eight-byte header and a two-byte trailer to each packet.

senses.definition: To load on a trailer or to transport by trailer.
examples: The engine wouldn't run any more so we had to trailer my old car to the wrecking yard.
